rationale: Evidence from R2A: all 60 development trials ended off_track with no completions. Progress was only 0.04 to 0.11, rms_error about 0.03 m, max_error about 0.06 m (the off-track limit is 0.06 m for this body), and line_loss_events averaged 1.0 per run. The robot leaves the line early, not late, and the failure is steering, not speed. The baseline's kp of 1.5 with coarse weights [-2,-1,0,1,2] gives a weak steering response, so the robot drifts outward on bends until it loses the tape, then the last_direction search at 0.35 throttle carries it off. Changes: (1) kp raised from 1.5 to 2.5 for stronger correction on bends; (2) kd raised from 0.1 to 0.4 to damp the faster response and limit overshoot; (3) ki set to 0 to avoid integral windup on curves where the signal stays one-sided; (4) base_speed lowered from 1.6 to 1.3 so the robot has time to correct at each bend, since finishing time is secondary until it stays on the line; (5) sensor_size raised from 12 mm to 16 mm so at least one sensor keeps reading tape through small lateral offsets and line loss becomes rarer; (6) sensors moved forward to y = 0.06 so they see the line earlier and the steering command leads the wheels; (7) mass lowered to 0.6 kg to reduce yaw inertia and speed up turn response. Expected result: fewer line-loss events, lower max_error, and the first completions on the oval and s-bend; the slalom is the most likely to still fail. Hypotheses to test: H1, if max_error stays near 0.06 with few line losses, steering gain is still too low, so raise kp toward 3.5. H2, if steering_oscillation is high with kp 2.5, kd is too low or the sensors are too far ahead, so raise kd or move sensors back. H3, if line_loss_events are still 1 per run at a fixed track position, the search mode is the issue, so test search_right or stop. Measurements wanted next: progress and completion_time for speed headroom, max_error and line_loss_events for steering margin, and steering_oscillation for damping.
